look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: crowding of comparatively SHORT radiating racemes is a useful first clue to hooded windmillgrass, but the strong confirmation is an unusually swollen round HOOD formed by the UPPER STERILE LEMMA on a mature spikelet. The existing photographs show a fresh radiating cluster and dry shorter branches, not a measured tiny hood; never label a whole raceme as a hood.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted POWO species and Texas state-level native distribution; source-pool admission approved; three target-zone county confirmations not independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial windmillgrass with short racemes in crowded whorls.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Fertile lemma ~1.5–2 mm with very short awn ~0.3–1.5 mm; sterile upper lemma swollen/hooded ~1–1.5 mm, awn absent or ≤1.5 mm.
best_field_traits: Inflated, rounded hood on the upper sterile lemma
Very short awns on both fertile and sterile florets
crew_field_walkthrough: Inspect the short crowded radiating branches on the flowering head, and photograph exactly where they arise.
Look at the dry hand-held specimen where individual spikelet-bearing branch segments are more distinct.
Isolate a mature spikelet under 10–20×: confirm swollen upper sterile lemma (roughly 1–1.5 mm), relatively short awns, and compare with a true C. verticillata specimen.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: One complete mature head showing short crowded racemes and their actual attachments.
Two mature upper sterile lemmas face-on and side-on with millimeter scale showing true swollen hood.
Fertile lemma short awn measured separately from the upper sterile lemma's awn.
Matched head-plus-spikelet images of C. verticillata and C. × subdolichostachya.
morphology_keys.field_photo_limitations: The hood is a tiny upper sterile LEMMA, not a whole spikelet or visibly inflated green inflorescence; source determination kept provisional.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. cucullata has congested short racemes and an inflated, nearly round upper sterile lemma with short awn; C. verticillata typically has separated tiers of longer racemes and distinctly longer awns. The hybrid may be intermediate and needs true spikelet confirmation; C. virgata is typically annual with a terminal feathery fan and long apical fertile-lemma hairs.
comparisons.cautions: Head color, overall windmill appearance and awn length alone can mislead. Inspect a fully mature spikelet with scale; hybrid intermediates must remain uncertain.

diagnostic_image_needs: Whole mature head and basal crown with scale
Dissected mature fertile and sterile lemmas with millimeter scale
Matched local Chloris comparison showing diagnostic whorl and awn differences

visual_comparison.title: Chloris cucullata — windmillgrass field ID
visual_comparison.subtitle: Actual installed photographs checked for visible structures; an image of a different species is explicitly labeled look-alike. Do not mislabel a whole raceme as a microscopic lemma.

items.label: 1 · Short radiating branches in a crowded head
items.image_role: Photo shows short crowded radiating racemes and their central junction
items.caption: The main Chloris head has multiple narrow radiating racemes at right, many with short spikelets. A separate dense foreground structure is not used for the hood diagnosis. The diagnostic inflated upper sterile lemma is NOT shown.
items.why_it_matters: The distinction between whole flowering head and a microscopic sterile lemma matters.

items.why_it_matters: Shows why broad seedhead shape alone often cannot prove the exact species.
